title: Post-Burnout Re-entry: Establishing Evidence-led Capacity Management
context: A managerial-level professional re-entering the workplace following burnout-related leave, facing challenges in rhythm recalibration and energy sustainability.
challenge: Perceiving workload as an uncontrollable external stressor, coupled with a lack of structured monitoring tools to identify and mitigate early exhaustion signals.
coaching_pivot: The coaching value focused on implementing a 'Capacity Auditing' system. By converting subjective fatigue into observable data points, we enabled the client to engage in objective stakeholder negotiations regarding sustainable output.
action: Execution of weekly energy audits; design of metric-driven phased return milestones; rehearsal of scripts for requesting technical support and naming professional boundaries.
results: Shift from reactive bracing to proactive capacity management. Improved ability to articulate professional needs through data rather than emotional appeal.
outcome: Secured a formal, phased re-entry agreement with management and established an enduring internal ritual for monitoring career sustainability.
timeframe: 6 sessions over 9 weeks with integrated asynchronous capacity check-ins.
disclaimer: Anonymised composite study for professional illustration.
